key_insight: T2D-Bench tests whether diabetes-focused LLM answers can prove they are supported by explicit, graph-checkable evidence instead of merely sounding clinically fluent.
clinical_relevance: This matters because unsupported medication or lifestyle guidance in type 2 diabetes can miss guideline constraints or make unjustified glycemic claims.
method: Built a multi-layer knowledge graph combining UMLS, DrugBank, SIDER, ADA guideline rules, and lifestyle-to-glycemia links
Evaluated LLM outputs on 100 structured vignettes covering diagnosis, medication safety, and adversarial lifestyle conflicts
Applied an evidence gate plus constrained revision to check and improve evidence-path compliance
evidence_signal: In the abstract, baseline outputs failed benchmark-defined evidence-path checks in 35% of cases for GPT-4o-mini and 33% for GPT-4o.
watch_item: The benchmark depends on the coverage and correctness of the underlying knowledge graph and rule encoding, so gaps there could affect what counts as evidence-compliant.
paper_title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
